confidence.rationale: Identity and the linked Toast catalog were independently reopened. The official Eat page exposes multiple service menus, two linked service pages could not be independently retrieved, and the accessible official PDF is a different, incomplete service-period catalog. findings.summary: Frozen rows label Toast/PDF-derived allergen arrays as official ingredient or official product-allergen evidence, but independently reopened sources provide menu descriptions only. Toast is restaurant-linked vendor, the PDF is restaurant-issued menu text, and neither is an allergen matrix or complete ingredient source. All frozen negative/complete-array semantics and all may-contain arrays are unverifiable.

Luna's zero-product catalog is materially incomplete. The independently reopened linked Toast catalog contains many food/nonalcoholic products, while the official Eat page also exposes linner and ready-to-go service surfaces not enumerated by Luna.

The accessible official PDF cannot be treated as the complete current menu: it differs from Toast and contains seasonal/general listings. It does, however, establish narrow positive evidence that beignets are fried in 100% refined peanut oil; this is not a negative, may-contain, or cross-contact conclusion.

The frozen data conflates generic/category rows, duplicate presentations, and service-specific products. Examples include Cold Grab & Go Retail Foods, Pop-Up Specials, Greens, New Orleans {3}, multiple J. Baker pimiento-cheese presentations, and differing waffle/quiche/mac-and-cheese fillings.
